description: Cross-implementation vectors for the alcove-signed-receipt/v4 step: ECDSA over P-256 with SHA-256 across the signer-bound receipt content. Each vector fixes a private key, an identity, a session key, a handshake role, and the shared content. The certificate fingerprint and the per-exchange binder are known answers. The signature is NOT -- ECDSA signing is randomized -- so it is verify-only and was produced by the openssl CLI (see externalAnchors) over signed bytes the generator assembles from the spec: a suite that accepts it is accepting a signature made outside this codebase, over a byte layout stated independently of the module under test. Regenerate with generate-signed-receipt-vectors.mjs.

construction.signedBytes: canonicalBytes({ domain: contentDomain, content: { termsHash, initiatorToResponderPayload, responderToInitiatorPayload, binder }, signer: { fingerprint, role } }) (RFC 8785)
construction.signatureEncoding: 64 bytes, r || s, each field element left-padded to 32 bytes. Not DER: a field of any other length is rejected rather than decoded.

vectors.name: initiator-both-directions
vectors.description: The initiator signs the receipt content bound to its own fingerprint and initiator role: the agreed-terms hash, the two directional session-keyed payload MACs (initiator->responder and responder->initiator, here fixed stand-in values), and the initiator-role binder. Any implementation given this private key, session key, and content must reproduce the fingerprint and the binder, and must accept the checked-in signature.

vectors.name: responder-distinct-identity
vectors.description: The responder signs the same directional content bound to its own fingerprint and responder role (both parties key the two directions identically). Uses the same session key but a distinct identity; its role names the responder-role binder derivation to pin that label too. That responder-role binder is a derivation not produced in a live exchange, where both parties fold in the initiator-role binder -- the vector pins the label for cross-implementation coverage.

bundle.description: A complete dual-signed record assembled from the two vectors above: both parties sign ONE shared content carrying the initiator-role binder, as a live exchange does. Every signature in it -- each certificate's self-signature and each party's receipt signature -- was produced by the openssl CLI (see externalAnchors), so an implementation that verifies this record is verifying a bundle no part of which it signed. The two fingerprints are the deterministic anchors a verifier pins against.

externalAnchors.note: Every checked-in signature was produced by the openssl CLI named above (openssl dgst -sha256 -sign, DER read back through openssl asn1parse and re-encoded as the fixed-length raw r||s), over signed bytes this generator assembles from docs/spec/EXCHANGE_RECORD.md. A suite that verifies them is therefore accepting a signature produced outside this codebase, over a byte layout stated independently of signedReceipt.ts. The same holds for every signature in the assembled bundle.
